title: Church website development | Creosote Labs
meta_description: Creosote Labs builds church websites with service times, sermons, giving links, event sign-ups, and forms. Fixed price, quoted after a scoping call.
h1: Website and web application development for churches
intro: Most churches maintain a website that carries service times, directions, staff, a statement of beliefs, sermon audio or video, and a link to online giving. Many were built on Squarespace, WordPress, or a church-specific builder years ago and are updated by a volunteer. Alongside the site there are usually separate forms for event registration, childcare sign-ups, prayer requests, and small-group sign-ups, plus a YouTube or Facebook feed for the live stream, each managed in its own place.

Creosote Labs builds a church website that a staff member or volunteer can update without a developer: service times and events on the home page, a sermon archive that pulls from the church's existing YouTube or podcast feed, and a giving link to Tithe.ly, Pushpay, or whichever platform the church uses. We also build the forms and tools behind the site, such as event registration with payment, a prayer request queue for the pastoral team, and a members-only directory. Hosting, domain setup, and written handover documentation are included.
projects: A marketing site for a congregation with service times, location, staff, beliefs, and a plan-your-visit page.
A sermon library that publishes each week's message automatically from the church's YouTube channel with series, speaker, and passage filters.
An event registration tool for retreats and vacation Bible school with capacity limits, waitlists, and card payment.
A members portal where households update their contact information and view their own giving history.
A prayer request form that routes submissions privately to the pastoral staff instead of a shared inbox.

faqs.q: How is a church website priced?
faqs.a: Website and application projects are quoted after a scoping call. The price is fixed for the agreed scope, with no hourly billing.

faqs.q: Can the church keep its current domain and giving platform?
faqs.a: Yes. We configure the existing domain to point at the new site and link to the giving platform the church already uses; the giving account itself is not changed.

faqs.q: Who updates the site after it launches?
faqs.a: Church staff or volunteers. The site is built so that events, sermons, and announcements can be edited without code, and handover includes written instructions for those tasks.
